title: Section 9 CPC — Courts to try all civil suits unless barred

content.overview: Section 9 CPC is the general civil jurisdiction rule: courts try all suits of a civil nature unless cognizance is expressly or impliedly barred. CPC remains in force; BNSS does not repeal it.
content.study: Start with Section 9 whenever a civil court is asked to hear a dispute. Ask two questions. First, is the suit of a civil nature? Second, is cognizance expressly or impliedly barred by another statute or by an exclusive forum? An implied bar is not inferred from inconvenience. It requires a clear legislative scheme that ousts the civil court.

sections.heading: Practice point
sections.body: Plead the civil right, then the statute said to bar the suit. Do not treat a specialised tribunal as an automatic ouster without reading the ouster clause.
